key_insight: The paper proposes ecological foundation models that combine diverse ecological datasets with ecological theory. The goal is to enable predictions that generalize better across ecosystems, scales, and research settings.
problem_solved: Ecological data and theories are fragmented across sources, scales, and approaches, making broad, reliable predictions difficult.
method: Bring together large, multimodal ecological datasets.
Combine data-driven foundation models with ecological theory.
Aim for transferable predictions across ecological contexts; the provided abstract does not report implementation details or evaluation results.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this proposal highlights a domain-grounded approach to foundation models: integrate scientific theory alongside diverse training data. It points toward more generalizable ecological prediction, rather than demonstrating a validated model in the supplied excerpt.
visual_elements: Scattered dataset icons converging into one ecological foundation model.
Two input streams—multimodal data and ecological theory—merging into a shared model.
A scale ladder connecting organisms, populations, and ecosystems.
A transfer diagram showing one model supporting predictions across different habitats.
paper_authors: Ross J. Gardiner, Henry Cerbone, Hammed A. Akande, Carly H. Batist, Amber Cowans
